question: In which of the following media is the speed of sound the highest?
solution: The correct answer is __**Iron**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Speed of sound** is highest in **solids** compared to liquids and gases due to the dense molecular structure and strong intermolecular forces. • In **iron**, the speed of sound is approximately **5960 m/s**, which is significantly higher than in water or air. • Sound travels slower in liquids like **water** (approximately **1482 m/s**) because molecules are less tightly packed compared to solids. • In gases like **air** at room temperature, the speed of sound is much lower, around **343 m/s**, due to the sparse arrangement of molecules. • Sound cannot travel in a **vacuum** as there are no molecules to propagate the vibration. Hence, the speed of sound is effectively **zero** in a vacuum.
